correctness.rationale: Otsubo's displayed parameter relation gives the diagonal equation \(9\mu^{3}(\mu^{2}+\mu+1)=(\mu+2)^{3}\). Exact factorization produces \((\mu-1)(3\mu^{2}+2\mu+4)(3\mu^{2}+4\mu+2)\); \(\mu=1\) is singular, and the two quadratic factors give exactly four allowed complex parameters. Exact polynomial reduction of Otsubo's \(j\)-formula gives \(j=-32768\) and \(j=8000\). The packaged standard-library checker replays all algebraic identities. Otsubo's theorem then turns each diagonal correspondence point into a degree-\(3\) endomorphism with kernel \(X+Y+Z=0\).
risks: The checker verifies the derived algebra, not the general isogeny theorem.
The CM-discriminant labels rely on the cited standard CM table rather than a packaged Hilbert-class-polynomial derivation.

value.rationale: A complete fixed-locus classification is a natural structural invariant of the newly explicit cubic-AGM Hesse isogeny correspondence. It identifies exactly four marked Hesse parameters, collapses them to two CM isomorphism classes, and explains the level-structure selection among the four classical j-level self-3-isogeny types. The statement is exact and reusable in studying cycles, specializations, and finite-field reductions of the correspondence.
risks: The derivation is algebraically short; its significance depends on treating the literal Hesse parameter as meaningful level structure rather than only the unmarked j-invariant.
